items.title: Al Rose Interview, 1976-02-19
items.q: [INTERVIEWER] Do you know, Al, do you have any idea where Miles Davis was influenced at all by the same kinds of things that Bix Beiderbeck was, for instance, Debussy or...

ctx.x: Well, I would say that in the first place, there is no fitting him into the history as such in a schematic sense. Fundamentally, it appeared from recorded evidence, it would appear that Bix, in a sense, shared the unique quality of Louis Armstrong, or would have shared it had he gotten old enough. To do so, as a musician of that highly personal quality, as to be able to transcend most of the groups and circumstances with which and in which he played. And he seemed to be an extraordinary individual artist. Now,…
Do you know, Al, do you have any idea where Miles Davis was influenced at all by the same kinds of things that Bix Beiderbeck was, for instance, Debussy or...

Well, Miles Davis is not a very articulate guy. And not only that, but he doesn't actually talk very much anyhow. So that he will say things like, you know, given a question, what is it that makes you decide what you're going to play when you get up on the stand? He says, well, I just think about it, and if it seems cool, I play it. Of course, that tells you nothing. And I found that he always tended to be very responsive to things that he had never heard before. Anytime he ever heard anything new that he had not…
